events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.62)
events.body:
This file is a safety dispute: the rider states that during the trip the driver made comments about her body and asked for her number, and that she felt harassed and unsafe [F4][SAFE-1]. SAFE-1 covers exactly this class of allegation — harassment, unwanted advances, intimidation — and its condition is the appearance of such conduct in a complaint statement or driver statement, not the presence of a keyword-matched in-app message; the trace's threat-keyword check accordingly returns no evidence and the only permitted outcome in the trace is escalate [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. Under SAFE-1 I therefore do not rule on the merits, make no finding against the driver, and issue no monetary determination.

The recorded facts are thin and are set out here for the human reviewer. There are no in-app chat messages between rider and driver on this trip, so the alleged remarks, if made, were oral and are not captured in any system record [F3]. The only in-app statement from the driver is a denial: "I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened" [F4]. The rider's account of the body comments and the request for her number is a first-hand narrative that does not itself appear as a data record in the fact table; the complaint text filed with the case is the source of the allegation [F4]. Both advocates request escalation and the driver's advocate expressly asks that escalation not be recorded as a harassment finding, which I adopt [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

The trip data neither corroborates nor contradicts the verbal allegation, and I note it only so the reviewer does not read it either way. GPS shows 17.2 km actual against 17.3 km optimal, i.e. 0.1 km shorter than optimal and therefore no off-route segment [F1]; RD-1 is not engaged in this case and cannot be used to infer anything about spoken conduct [F1][RD-1]. Duration was 25.9 min against a 24 min estimate, a 2.3 min overrun [F2]; that is a timing residual, not evidence of unsafe driving, and no traffic or incident fact exists in the file to explain or weigh it [F2][SAFE-2]. The fare is a fixed RydeX quote ($35.84) with no deviation-driven item, so there is nothing refundable [F1][RD-2].

Profile facts are neutral and decide nothing here: the rider is a 3.8-year, 4.8-rated account with 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days [F5]; the driver is a 4.5-year, 4.86-rated account with 659 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes and 0 upheld [F6]. A clean history neither establishes nor defeats an incident-specific harassment allegation, and no account-level action is warranted on this record [F5][F6][RD-6].

Points a human reviewer should check: (1) whether any call, voice or in-app communication record exists outside the chat fact, which currently shows none [F3]; (2) the rider's contemporaneous account and whether she reported the conduct to RydeHELP near the trip time [F4]; (3) the driver's account beyond the denial and any prior conduct or safety reports on his account, since the profile shows 0 disputes in 90 days [F4][F6]; (4) the drop-off timeline (pickup 22:29, drop-off 22:54) against the rider's description of when the remarks occurred [F2]. Under SAFE-1 and NS-7 the human reviewer retains discretion; this output is a recommendation only.

No monetary adjustment; fare stands as billed.

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint is that the driver made comments about her body and asked for her number, and that she felt harassed and unsafe during the trip (chat/submission record F3, F4).

There are no in-app chat messages between rider and driver for this trip (F3), so the alleged harassment was spoken in the vehicle and is not captured in any system record; the only in-app statement is the driver's denial, 'I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened' (F4).

Harassment, unwanted advances and intimidation fall squarely within SAFE-1, which mandates escalate to human review rather than an automatic ruling; the rider's account of the driver's body comments and request for her number is exactly such an allegation.

Because SAFE-1 is engaged, the correct disposition is a human-handled escalation with a written fact summary, not a monetary determination; the rider does not seek a fare adjustment and the trip facts show no billing irregularity (F1, F2).

The GPS record shows the trip followed the optimal route (17.2 km actual vs 17.3 km optimal, F1) in 25.9 min against a 24 min estimate (F2), so nothing in the trip data contradicts the rider's account or suggests the ride itself was abnormal; the ride appeared normal while the rider's experience of it was not.

The rider has a 3.8-year account with a 4.8 rating and zero disputes or upheld complaints in 90 days (F5), and the driver likewise shows zero disputes and zero upheld complaints over 659 trips (F6); none of this hearsay-free history can decide the harassment question, but it supports treating the escalation as a good-faith report rather than abuse.

weaknesses: There is no system record of the alleged harassment: F3 confirms there were no in-app chat messages at all, so the rider's account rests on her own statement alone, while the driver's statement (F4) denies anything inappropriate. Under the rule that system records beat statements, the rider cannot prove the content of the conversation from the fact table.

No threat keyword or [threat]-tagged message exists in the chat record (F3), so SAFE-1 cannot be triggered by any objective marker in the data — only by the rider's narrative; the other side will argue the case is a bare assertion versus a denial.

The driver has a long, clean record — 4.5 years, 4.86 rating, 659 trips, 0 disputes (F6) — which the driver will use to argue the complaint is out of character; profile facts (F5, F6) cannot themselves establish or defeat the harassment claim.

claims.assertion: The rider's allegation is one of harassment ('comments about my body and asked for my number'), and the case file contains no chat evidence of any such remark: the only chat fact records that there were no in-app messages between rider and driver at all (F3), so the allegation rests on an untranscribed oral account. No SAFE-1 trigger (a chat-threat-* fact) exists in this file, and the driver's recorded statement is that he made small talk and nothing inappropriate happened (F4).

No objective trip record corroborates unsafe, abnormal or erratic conduct: the GPS track shows the trip was actually 0.1 km shorter than the optimal route, i.e. no deviation whatsoever (F1), so there is no off-route segment, no unexplained stop and no route-based safety concern to support a finding against the driver.

The only recorded deviation from plan is duration: 25.9 min against a 24 min estimate, a difference of 2.3 min on a 17.3 km trip (F2), which is consistent with ordinary traffic on a Woodlands-Punggol run and is a timing residual, not evidence of harassment or of any unsafe act.

The driver's account history gives no basis for an account-level finding: 4.5 years on the platform, rating 4.86, 659 trips in the last 90 days, and zero disputes with zero upheld in 90 days (F5, F6), so there is no 'repeated' conduct pattern to attach to this complaint.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint is a first-hand account of oral conduct; SAFE-1 expressly covers harassment appearing in a complaint statement, not only in chat, and F3 merely shows the exchange was not in-app, so the absence of chat records does not disprove that anything was said. The rider is a 3.8-year account holder rated 4.8 with 0 disputes in 90 days (F5), so she has no history of inventing complaints to discount her.

There is no recording, transcript or third-party witness in the file, so the driver's denial (F4) and the rider's account can only be weighed against each other, not resolved by a system record — precisely the situation in which the file is thinnest for the driver.

If the adjudicator treats the complaint statement itself as sufficient to raise a safety event, SAFE-1 routes the file to escalate rather than to no_action, which means the driver gets no clean dismissal and the matter stays open for a human reviewer.

points.response: D1 concedes the decisive point and then draws the wrong conclusion: SAFE-1 is triggered by threats, intimidation, harassment or unwanted advances appearing in the complaint statement, and it does not require a chat-threat-* fact in the file (SAFE-1); F3 shows only that the exchange was not in-app, which says nothing about what was said aloud, and the driver's denial in F4 is a party statement that cannot outweigh the complainant's own first-hand account.

D2 is void as against this case: RD-1 governs route deviation, which is not the dispute type here, and even on its own terms the GPS record it cites was produced by the driver's own track path (F1), a source that cannot evidence whether he made comments about the rider's body or asked for her number; a clean route no more disproves harassment than a clean speedometer disproves a threat.

D3 asserts the 2.3-minute excess (F2) is ordinary traffic, but the file contains no traffic or weather facts at all, so the traffic explanation is unsupported assertion, and in any event duration is irrelevant: the rider's complaint is about verbal conduct, which no timing record can capture.

D4 is correct that F5 and F6 show no pattern (659 trips, 0 disputes, F6), but a clean history is not a defence: SAFE-1 applies to the incident alleged, and the rider's 3.8-year, 4.8-rated, dispute-free account (F5) equally shows she has no record of inventing complaints, so history-neutrality leaves the allegation standing for human review.

The driver's clean record (F6) is relevant only to whether any account-level action is warranted, and it is precisely why the rider does not seek flag_account; what the rider seeks is that the safety complaint be escalated for human investigation, which is the disposition SAFE-1 mandates.

I do not contest that this is the rider's complaint, but the only two facts in the file are that no in-app chat exists (F3) and the driver's denial (F4); the rider's account of what was said is a narrative located outside the fact table, so it cannot be weighed against the driver's equally unrecorded statement on this record.

Conceded: there is no system record of the alleged words and no [threat]-tagged message (F3), so the harassment question turns on an unsupported allegation against a specific denial (F4) — a tie in the record that SAFE-1 resolves only by sending the file to a human, which is what both sides in fact request.

I do not dispute that SAFE-1 requires escalation rather than an automatic ruling, but escalation is a routing decision, not a finding: it leaves the driver's account intact and must not be recorded as a harassment finding against him, since the record contains no corroboration beyond an untranscribed oral account (F3, F4).

Agreed that no monetary determination arises — the trip was billed at a fixed RydeX fare with 17.2 km actual against 17.3 km optimal (F1) and 25.9 min against a 24 min estimate (F2), so there is no refundable item for the rider to recover; I ask that the escalation be equally neutral as to the driver.

The rider's own reading of the trip data defeats any suggestion of unsafe or abnormal driving: the route was 0.1 km shorter than optimal with no off-route segment (F1), and a 2.3 min overrun on a 17.3 km trip (F2) is ordinary traffic variance — nothing here supports a driving-conduct concern, only an unresolved oral allegation.

The rider's clean history (F5) does not add corroboration to her account, and the driver's equally clean record — 4.5 years, 4.86 rating, 659 trips, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days (F6) — means good faith cuts both ways and cannot tip the harassment question either way.
